mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2% for two consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 2% and remains above for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during the previous 20-day window with similar FEDFUNDS path (t-test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment rates (UNRATE) reduce consumer and business confidence, lowering expected future corporate earnings and driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative relative to the 60-day window before UNRATE crossed 6.5% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in housing starts (HOUST) signals reduced near-term demand for consumer and business fixed assets, which predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls by more than 15% in a single month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not lower than the preceding 5-day window with similar HOUST decline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below 50 for two consecutive months indicates weakening supply capacity, which tends to depress equity valuations and produce negative 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain non-negative in at least 70% of INDPRO contraction episodes (empirical frequency).

mechanism_narrative: When the ratio of consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) to GDP deflator (not in catalog, so use CPIAUCSL alone) accelerates above 2% for three months, it suggests accelerating inflation expectations that coincide with negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL monthly growth rate exceeds 2% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative relative to the prior 20-day window with similar CPIAUCSL growth (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising payrolls (PAYEMS) above 200,000 but persistently high unemployment (UNRATE > 5%), indicate a labor market that is expanding too slowly to sustain equity valuations, predicting negative 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 200,000 and UNRATE > 5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically negative in 80% of such labor market episodes (empirical frequency).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in retail sales proxy (not available - use GDPC1 as a demand proxy instead) so using GDPC1 decline of 10% in a month predicts negative 20-day S&P 500 returns due to reduced consumer demand.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls by more than 10% in a single month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative relative to the prior 20-day window with similar GDPC1 decline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS rising while UNRATE < 4%), S&P 500 20-day forward returns tend to be flat or negative due to higher discount rates and reduced risk appetite.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rising trend and UNRATE below 4% for 3 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not negative in > 70% of tightening cycles (measured by rolling window regression).
